paper.title_en: From the massive Schwinger model to unimodular Euclidean gravity with fermions
paper.abstract_en: The massive Schwinger model (two-dimensional electrodynamics coupled to Dirac fermions) in Euclidean spacetime is mapped onto two-dimensional unimodular gravity in the first-order formalism, also including fermions. The idea of the map relies almost entirely on the isomorphism between the gauge groups $U(1)$ and $SO(2)$. However, the resulting fermion-gravity coupling differs from the conventional form, explicitly violating parity and time-reversal symmetries. Moreover, these fermions exhibit an unconventional transformation behavior under $SO(2)$ transformations. We show, however, that these properties are absent on the gravitational side of the mapping when starting from an axial massive Schwinger model. Several explicit examples of the mapping are considered, including the constant electric field and point-particle systems. For these examples, we explicitly derive the corresponding gravitational manifolds and compute the associated metrics. Furthermore, we analyze the consistency of the mapping at the quantum level using the path-integral formalism and Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin (BRST) techniques. Our results demonstrate that the proposed mapping remains consistent at the quantum level, establishing a formal BRST-compatible field correspondence between quantum electrodynamics and quantum gravity, at least at the $U(1) - SO(2)$ gauge sector, which does not include the diffeomorphic features of gravity.
